question.worked_solution:
First, let's remove the negative sign from the variable. To do this, we multiply both sides of the equation by $-1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{c}{12} & =4 \\ (-1)\cdot (-\frac{c}{12}) & =(-1)\cdot 4 \\ \frac{c}{12} & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

In the equation above, $c$ is being divided by $12.$ To isolate $c$, we can perform the opposite operation, which is *multiplying* by $12.$ So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $12$ and simplify.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{c}{12} & =-4 \\ 12\cdot \frac{c}{12} & =12\cdot (-4) \\ \frac{12c}{12} & =-48 \\ \frac{\cancel{12}c}{\cancel{12}} & =-48 \\ c & =-48\end{aligned}
$$
